label: Person
name: Agostino Rivarola
summary:
Agostino Rivarola (1758–1842) was an Italian cardinal who served the papacy during one of its most turbulent periods, including the Napoleonic suppression of papal authority and the subsequent restoration. Born in Genoa, he pursued an ecclesiastical career in Rome and was appointed a cardinal by Pope Pius VII, serving in key roles during the period of French occupation of the Papal States.

Rivarola's career spanned the extraordinary upheavals of the Napoleonic era: the French invasion of Italy, the imprisonment of Pope Pius VII by Napoleon, the forced exile of the Roman Curia, and the eventual restoration of the papacy after Napoleon's defeat. He served as one of the cardinals who maintained continuity of Catholic administration during these extreme conditions, navigating between loyalty to the imprisoned pope and the practical necessities of French-occupied Rome.

After the Restoration, Rivarola served as a senior figure in the reconstituted Papal States administration. His long career bridged the ancien régime Church, the Napoleonic disruption, and the Restoration, making him a figure of institutional continuity across one of Catholicism's most dramatically unstable periods. He died in Rome in 1842, having witnessed eighty years of extraordinary transformation in the Church's political situation.
